statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-34077 (GHSA-rxv8-25v2-qmq8) is a denial-of-service flaw in turbo-stream's flatten/unflatten serialization, reachable only through its encode/decode entry points. Trigger.dev's self-hosted webapp (apps/webapp) is a Remix v2 application (@remix-run/* 2.17.4); turbo-stream is pulled in transitively only by @remix-run/server-runtime and @remix-run/react, which import it solely from their Single Fetch helpers (single-fetch.js: encodeViaTurboStream / decodeViaTurboStream). Those helpers are invoked by the Remix router only when Single Fetch is enabled. The shipped apps/webapp/remix.config.js at v4.4.6 declares no `future` block and does not set future.unstable_singleFetch, so Single Fetch is disabled (the Remix v2 default) and the router never reaches turbo-stream's encode/decode. The vulnerable code is present in the image but is never in the execute path. The only upstream fix is turbo-stream 3.0.0, a breaking major release: @remix-run/server-runtime and @remix-run/react pin turbo-stream to exactly 2.4.1, and 3.0.0 changes the encode/decode stream types and signatures and removes the postPlugins option, so it cannot be adopted without breaking Remix v2's Single Fetch contract.
